summary: The root خمص (khmS) primarily describes emptiness or hunger, especially of the belly. It can refer to a person who is hungry or lank, and metaphorically, one who abstains from others' possessions.
lane: خَمِيصٌ خميص Empty; applied to the belly: (TA:) hungry. (Msb.) -b2- خَمِيصُ البَطْنِ , (A,) or خَمِيصُ الحَشَا , (S, K,) and , (S, A, K,) and , (A, K,) A man empty in the belly, (A,) or lank in the belly; (S, K;) as also البَطْنِ : (K * and TA in art. رهف :) and slender in make: (TA:) fem. of the first with ة , (S, A, K,) and so of the second, (Yaakoob, S, A, K,) and so of the third; (TA;) and IAar mentions as a fem., occurring prefixed to الحَشَا in a verse of El-Asamm Ed-Dubeyree: (TA:) pl., (S, A, K,) masc., (A, K,) خِمَاصٌ ; (S, A, K;) and fem., [i. e., of خميصة ,] خَمَائِصُ : (A, K:) has no pl. formed by the addition of و and ن , though its fem. is formed by the addition of ة ; being made to accord with the measure فَعْلَانٌ , of which the fem. is فَعْلَى . (TA.) خِمَاصٌ [also] signifies Hungry, in a pl. sense, (K,) and lank in the bellies: (TA:) also signifies the same as خَمِيصٌ ; and [its pl.] مَخَامِيصُ , lank in the bellies ( خُمْصُ البُطُونِ [whence it appears that , sing. of خُمْصٌ , is also syn. with خَمِيصٌ ]). (TA.) You say also, هُوَ خَمِيصُ البَطْنِ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ , meaning (tropical:) He is one who abstains from [ devouring ] the possessions of men. (A.) And خِمَاصُ البُطُونِ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ خِفَافُ الظُّهُورِ مِنْ دَمَائِهِمْ , (A, TA,) meaning (tropical:) Persons who abstain from [ devouring ] the possessions of men, whose backs are light with respect to [ the ] burden [ of their blood ]. (TA, from a trad.) -b3- زَمَنٌ خَمِيصٌ (tropical:) A time of hunger. (A, TA.)
